issues.description: Element: bytes-per-pixel used for address calculation (logical pixel size). Problem statement: lines state pixels are rounded to 32 bits (4 bytes per pixel). Template/main usage: the program's stride and comments expect 4 bytes per pixel (row stride = 1920 * 4 = 7680). Solution implementation: set_pixel routine multiplies x by 3 (mov edx, 3; mul edx) and uses x*3 in the address computation, effectively assuming 3 bytes per pixel. How it blocks students: this contradiction between the problem text/template (4 bytes) and the solution code (3 bytes) will produce incorrect addresses and corrupted writes, and forces students to guess whether to use 3 or 4 bytes per pixel when implementing the missing code.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution implementation consistent with the specification (4 bytes per pixel). In the solution's set_pixel routine replace the x*3 multiplication with x*4 (e.g. use shl eax, 2 or multiply by 4) and compute the address as display_start + y*(1920*4) + x*4 (equivalently display_start + y*7680 + x*4). Then write the 32-bit RGB value at that address (mov [address], ecx). Also preserve registers according to the exercise constraints (only allow eax to be clobbered or push/pop registers you modify) so the routine matches the problem's register-preservation requirements.
